<a data-pjax="true" title="feat: support client-side roaring bitmap blobs for roaring_match (#3764)

`roaring_match(field, {ids})` is the exact-membership sibling of
`bloom_match`, added server-side in milvus-io/milvus#51968 (merged). The
client compresses a membership set into a roaring bitmap and ships the
blob as a template value, so a set that would blow past the proxy's gRPC
receive limit as an `in [...]` list rides the wire in a fraction of the
space — and, unlike a bloom filter, with no false positives, which is
why the server also permits it in delete expressions.

The expression accepts **only** a `{template}` placeholder resolving to
protobuf `bytes` holding a complete MRB1 blob. There is no literal-list
form. So without an SDK-side builder the feature is unreachable from
Python entirely.

## What this adds

- `pymilvus/client/roaring_filter.py` — `build_roaring_bitmap(members)
-> bytes` and a streaming `RoaringBitmapBuilder`, both exported from
`pymilvus/__init__.py` next to `build_bloom_filter` /
`BloomFilterBuilder`.
- 180 tests plus the shared cross-SDK golden vectors, beside the bloom
fixture.

No new dependency, and the template path is **not** touched: the bytes
branch added for `bloom_match` in #3690 already carries the blob
unchanged through query, search and delete. A test asserts that end of
it rather than re-plumbing it.

## Why no pyroaring dependency

Most roaring libraries' default serialization is *not* the portable
format segcore decodes — that mismatch is the documented trap in the
design doc. The writer is ~200 lines and the client only ever writes,
never parses, so hand-writing it avoids a native dependency and a
serialization dialect we don't control.

## Usage

```python
from pymilvus import build_roaring_bitmap

ids = build_roaring_bitmap([-7, 42, 1001])          # reuse this across queries
client.query(
    collection_name="docs",
    filter="roaring_match(creator_id, {ids})",
    filter_params={"ids": ids},
)
```

Building the blob is the expensive part, so it is meant to be built once
and reused — that amortization is the entire point of the feature. For a
set that arrives in pieces,
`RoaringBitmapBuilder().add_int64_batch(page)` avoids ever materializing
the full member list.

## Verification

The bytes must match what every other SDK produces, so conformance is
byte-identity against the Go reference (`client/roaringfilter.Build`),
not just "the server accepts it":

- **29/29 shared golden vectors byte-identical**, sha256 included, plus
the fixture's own container decomposition (high/low container counts and
array/bitmap/run kinds) checked against the builder's.
- **300/300 additional randomized cases byte-identical** to the Go
reference, on inputs not in the fixture set.
- The fixtures themselves were verified to pass the server's own
validator and to decode under CRoaring — the library segcore probes with
— with exact membership.
- A test-only reader recovers the exact member set from all 29 blobs and
from randomized shapes.
- 19 deliberate mutations each turned a test red, including the
tie-break constant, a 2^63-biased mapping, 32-bit key truncation,
dropped/misplaced offset tables, off-by-one descriptors and run lengths,
MSB-first bitmap and run-bitmap writes, and signed sorting during
builder compaction.

One subtlety worth flagging for reviewers: the run-vs-bitmap tie-break
compares against **8224**, not 8192. That is the reference's in-memory
`bitmapContainerSizeInBytes()` (`unsafe.Sizeof(bitmapContainer{}) +
65536/8`). Using 8192 flips the encoding for containers with 2048..2055
runs *when the array encoding is larger still*, and desynchronizes this
SDK's bytes from every other one. The `run_bitmap_tiebreak_run` /
`run_bitmap_tiebreak_bitmap` vectors sit either side of it.

## An honest note on one mutation

`np.dtype("u2")` vs `np.dtype("<u2")` is an **equivalent mutant at
runtime on a little-endian host** — numpy resolves the native form
eagerly, so `np.dtype("u2") is np.dtype("<u2")` is literally `True` and
no runtime assertion can distinguish them. (The `newbyteorder` guard in
the bloom tests has the same blind spot.) It is a real bug on a
big-endian client, which is exactly what #3690's third review round was
about. It is pinned here by a test that greps the module source for
`np.dtype("…")` literals and requires the explicit `<`.

## Tests

```
PYTHONPATH=$PWD uv run --group dev pytest tests/unit/test_roaring_filter.py -q   # 180 passed
PYTHONPATH=$PWD uv run --group dev pytest tests/unit -q                          # 4716 passed, 3 skipped
make lint                                                                        # clean
```

Baseline before this change was 4536 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed, so
there are no pre-existing failures in play.

Design doc:
`docs/design-docs/design_docs/20260714-roaring-exact-membership-expression.md`
in milvus-io/milvus.

---------

<a data-pjax="true" title="feat: support client-side roaring bitmap blobs for roaring_match (#3764)

`roaring_match(field, {ids})` is the exact-membership sibling of
`bloom_match`, added server-side in milvus-io/milvus#51968 (merged). The
client compresses a membership set into a roaring bitmap and ships the
blob as a template value, so a set that would blow past the proxy's gRPC
receive limit as an `in [...]` list rides the wire in a fraction of the
space — and, unlike a bloom filter, with no false positives, which is
why the server also permits it in delete expressions.

The expression accepts **only** a `{template}` placeholder resolving to
protobuf `bytes` holding a complete MRB1 blob. There is no literal-list
form. So without an SDK-side builder the feature is unreachable from
Python entirely.

## What this adds

- `pymilvus/client/roaring_filter.py` — `build_roaring_bitmap(members)
-> bytes` and a streaming `RoaringBitmapBuilder`, both exported from
`pymilvus/__init__.py` next to `build_bloom_filter` /
`BloomFilterBuilder`.
- 180 tests plus the shared cross-SDK golden vectors, beside the bloom
fixture.

No new dependency, and the template path is **not** touched: the bytes
branch added for `bloom_match` in #3690 already carries the blob
unchanged through query, search and delete. A test asserts that end of
it rather than re-plumbing it.

## Why no pyroaring dependency

Most roaring libraries' default serialization is *not* the portable
format segcore decodes — that mismatch is the documented trap in the
design doc. The writer is ~200 lines and the client only ever writes,
never parses, so hand-writing it avoids a native dependency and a
serialization dialect we don't control.

## Usage

```python
from pymilvus import build_roaring_bitmap

ids = build_roaring_bitmap([-7, 42, 1001])          # reuse this across queries
client.query(
    collection_name="docs",
    filter="roaring_match(creator_id, {ids})",
    filter_params={"ids": ids},
)
```

Building the blob is the expensive part, so it is meant to be built once
and reused — that amortization is the entire point of the feature. For a
set that arrives in pieces,
`RoaringBitmapBuilder().add_int64_batch(page)` avoids ever materializing
the full member list.

<a data-pjax="true" title="chore: use hatchling version source (#3528)

## Summary
- switch the build backend from setuptools to hatchling
- use Hatch's code version source to keep the existing rc-distance
version scheme without a root-level _version_helper.py or setup.py
- use the hatchling CLI for version detection in Makefile and the Milvus
update workflow
- remove the obsolete manifest include for _version_helper.py
- add focused tests for the rc version scheme

## Version behavior
- non-tag builds continue to resolve to rc-distance versions, e.g.
3.1.0rc16
- exact tag builds continue to resolve to the tag version

<a data-pjax="true" title="feat: support bloom_match filter parameters (#3690)

## Summary

Adds PyMilvus support for the `bloom_match(field, {blob})` expression
introduced by milvus-io/milvus#51140.

- exports `build_bloom_filter(members, fpr=0.005)`, a dependency-free
MBF1 / Parquet Split-Block Bloom filter builder for homogeneous `int`
(signed int64) or `str` members;
- encodes the resulting blob as native `TemplateValue.bytes_val`, with
no base64 expansion;
- updates the `milvus-proto` submodule and generated Python stubs to
proto #632, which added `TemplateValue.bytes_val`;
- proves byte-for-byte parity against canonical int64 and Unicode-string
golden vectors plus a checked-in Apache Arrow C++ fixture containing 100
deterministic random int64 members.

## Dependencies

- Server feature: milvus-io/milvus#51140
- Proto field: milvus-io/milvus-proto#632
- Design: [Bloom Filter Membership
Expression](https://github.com/xiaofan-luan/milvus/blob/feat-bloom-filter-expr/docs/design-docs/design_docs/20260707-bloom-filter-expression.md)

## Validation

<p dir="auto">Q5. How to set up pre-commit hooks to automatically check and fix the coding styles?</p>
<p dir="auto">
Once installed, the hooks will automatically run 
<code>make format</code>
 and 
<code>make lint</code>
 before each commit. If the checks fail, the commit will be aborted, and you'll need to fix the issues before committing again.
</p>

<p dir="auto">
The commits on the development branch of each version will be packaged and uploaded to 
<a href="https://test.pypi.org/" rel="nofollow">Test PyPI</a>
.
</p>
<p dir="auto">The package name generated by the development branch is x.y.z.rc, where  is the number of commits that differ from the most recent release.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto">
For example, after the release of 
<strong>2.3.4</strong>
, two commits were submitted on the 2.3 branch.
The version number of the latest commit of 2.3 branch is 
<strong>2.3.5.rc2</strong>
.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">
For example, after the release of 
<strong>2.3.4</strong>
, 10 commits were submitted on the master branch.
The version number of the latest commit of master branch is 
<strong>2.4.0.rc10</strong>
.
</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">
To install the package on Test PyPi, you need to append 
<code>--extra-index-url</code>
 after pip, for example:
</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto">
<pre>$ python3 -m pip install --extra-index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ pymilvus==2.1.0.dev66</pre>
